answer: Random jury of 9 drawn without replacement at the quill: a farm holding k% of identities lands a fully-corrupt panel only k^9 of the time. The vertex enforces BFT quorum independence — each seat sampled from disjoint stake, so collusion can't reuse one identity twice. A farm at 30% wins a jury 0.0002% of rounds; the comet of slashed bonds burns before recouping. Sampling randomness is the check; quadratic collapse is the consequence. It works because honest supermajority holds while sybil cost scales exponentially against linear reward.
